title: Claustodian Symbol Record
description: One trackable Claude Code symbol (a CLI flag, environment variable, command, config key, internal config flag, stream-json control message, mods API method, mods event, mods render site, mods element, hook event, or model), along with its lifecycle metadata and provenance.

symbol.description: The exact flag/var/command/key name, e.g. "--safe-mode" or "CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE".

type.description: The kind of symbol this record describes. A mod_event is a name a mod passes to on(), such as tool.call. Every mod_method is also an event of the same name without the $. prefix; such an event has a mod_event record only when the docs also list it as an event, as they do ui.close. A mod_render_site is a place a mod can draw, the value of e.component in a ui.render hook, such as AbovePrompt. A mod_element is a node type a ui.render tree is built from, such as Box. A hook_event is a point in a session where a hook from the hooks setting can run, such as PreToolUse. A model is a Claude model the CLI knows, by its first-party API id, such as claude-opus-5-5.

first_seen.description: Claude Code version where this symbol was first observed (not necessarily first existed; see project README). When `first_seen_estimated` is true this is an upper bound, not a confirmed introduction.

removed_in.description: Version where the symbol disappeared, if known; null otherwise.

deprecated_in.description: Version whose official changelog deprecated the symbol. Present only when the symbol has been deprecated; the symbol still exists (status is `deprecated` in snapshots at/after this version, `active` before).

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the symbol.

provenance.description: Where the symbol's existence was established: an official changelog entry, an official docs reference page, or binary/bundle string extraction.

confidence.description: Confidence in the accuracy of this record. For the changelog and docs lanes this tracks the date: "high" when first_seen is anchored (an introducing changelog bullet or an official docs min-version), "medium" when it is an estimate (see first_seen_estimated). control_message records are graded by EVIDENCE STRENGTH instead, then capped: "high" for a described schema declaration, "low" for a subtype evidenced only by a dispatch, and any "high" is lowered to "medium" when first_seen is an upper bound. So a "low" control record may still be exactly dated — read first_seen_estimated for the date, not confidence.

description.description: Plain-language explanation of what the symbol does. Sourced from official docs when available (see description_source); may be empty when no authoritative description exists yet.

description_source.description: Where `description` came from: an official docs page, an introducing changelog bullet, the command/skill registry extracted from the binary, or the symbol's own `claude --help` output. Absent when the description is empty.

first_seen_estimated.description: True when `first_seen` is an upper bound (the symbol was observed by that version but its true introduction is unconfirmed), e.g. a symbol only ever named incidentally in the changelog or documented without a min-version. Corrected by the binary lane for those; SET by it for a control_message subtype that was declared before extraction could prove it. Absent means false.

source_url.description: Link to the changelog entry that introduced this symbol; null for binary-only finds.

category.description: Grouping used for topic (startup, networking, ui, filesystem, auth, ...), for ownership/source scoping (third-party, cloud-auth, ci-detect, runtime, terminal, ...), and for how a symbol is surfaced: `cli-internal` for a flag hidden from `claude --help`, `settings`/`settings-internal` for keys in settings.json, `global-config` for keys in ~/.claude.json.

family.description: The message family the CLI routes this subtype as. Only control_message records carry it. Membership is proven by the CLI dispatching the subtype on its control-request handler path, or by a union it routes as control requests — so a record can carry this value without any union naming it, which is the case for every subtype evidenced only by a call site or a dispatch. The enum widens if further families (system messages, control responses, result messages) are published later; the record `type` deliberately does not encode the family, so identity survives a reclassification.

direction.description: Which side of the stream-json channel sends this message. Derived only from the two disjoint sub-unions the bundle itself declares, never inferred from a call site's surroundings. Null means the direction is not observable for this record, which happens two ways: the version predates the split the CLI began declaring at 2.1.133, OR the subtype belongs to no directional sub-union in that version — true of every subtype evidenced only by a call site or a dispatch, at any version. Null is therefore NOT a statement that the CLI fails to distinguish the two directions, and it is never backfilled from a later version. Only control_message records carry it.

scopes.description: Subcommands this flag is accepted under, e.g. ["remote-control"] or ["mcp add","plugin install"]. Values are FULL invocation paths after `claude`. A bare parent is only correct when that invocation really accepts the flag: commander rejects a sub-subcommand's flag at its parent, so ["plugin"] alone is a false claim for a `plugin eval` flag — but a parent AND its child can both appear when both accept it, as `--hooks-dir` does. COMPLETE when present, so a non-empty list also means the flag is NOT accepted on bare `claude`. Absent means no scope information — not "top-level". Only cli_flag records carry it.

scope_descriptions.description: Per-scope description overrides for a `cli_flag`. Each key is an invocation path drawn from `scopes`, and its value is the flag's description under that scope. That keys are a subset of `scopes` is an invariant the generator enforces (the scrape lane intersects this map against the binary-proved `scopes`), not something this schema validates — JSON Schema cannot compare an object's keys to an array's items, so the schema requires only that `scopes` is present when this field is. Read `scope_descriptions[scope]`, and fall back to the top-level `description` for a scope not present here. Only cli_flag records carry it, in two cases. (1) The official docs document the flag differently under different subcommands — e.g. `--force` means "overwrite an existing .claude-plugin directory" under `plugin init` but "create the tag even if the working tree is dirty" under `plugin tag`. The top-level `description` stays the primary, and a scope with no documented override (e.g. `install`) is deliberately absent rather than given a wrong description. (2) A docs page that ties its sections to subcommands documents the flag under only some of the subcommands the binary shows. The docs text then appears here for the documented subcommands, and the top-level `description` is empty, so it describes no other subcommand (e.g. `--api-url`, documented for `self-hosted-runner` but also the JWKS endpoint under `self-hosted-runner decode-token`). Additive and optional.
